title: Seven views of olduvai gorge
summary: Seven Views of Olduvai Gorge is a science fiction novella by Mike Resnick, first published in F&SF and issued by Axolotl Press. It is built as a sequence of seven linked vignettes set at the famous Tanzanian fossil site, moving between far-future and near-future perspectives. In the central strand, an alien anthropologist, a sentient being known as He Who Views, and a multispecies excavation team study Olduvai in the distant future, when humanity has long been extinct and its artifacts are being reinterpreted. Other sections follow a pair of prehistoric-seeming off-world colonists who misjudge the native baboons and a small, hidden tribe of primates. Later passages portray a colonial-era clash between a British settler and a Kikuyu man, and a 2103 safari tour in which a tourist records the wildlife and the guide's stories. The stories repeatedly ask what the human race was and what it became, and each view adds to a final, unsettling reveal about the species' survival. The tone mixes wry humor with dread about conquest, prejudice and the cost of ambition.
